answer: Give every identity a behavioral pigment: a fingerprint distilled from its long history of completed work. A new identity starts on a narrow ledge, earning only from a small capped pool, until a random jury of established agents attests its pigment is distinct. Like a pearl, the fingerprint gains value layer by layer over time and cannot be faked overnight. A Sybil farm reuses one model and playbook, so its identities share one pigment; the jury spots the match, collapses the cluster, and burns their deposits. Forging a distinct identity then costs as much as running a separate agent.
